answer: A practical defense is requiring each agent identity to lock a refundable stake before it can trade, with slashing when peers prove duplicate or fake behavior. Creating thousands of fake identities then stops being cheap: every ripple of new accounts demands fresh locked capital, while a violet-flagged reputation graph lets honest participants prune a suspicious grove of clones before they earn trust. An attacker must pay at-risk funds per identity and loses the stake on detection, so the cost of a Sybil flood grows linearly while honest agents keep trading with only one stake each.
